minutes.headline: Select Board adopted a public communications policy 3-2 after one night's notice, and took no action on the Flat Hill Road petition.
minutes.summary: After a long executive session, the board appointed a Parks Commission member, approved a skate park toll booth fundraiser and new police sex offender policies, and heard a petition from Flat Hill Road residents seeking a lower speed limit. The board took no action pending a further traffic study. It discussed the interim and permanent town manager search and salary, adopted a new public communications policy over objections about process, and approved a letter to the state representative on Chapter 70 and bus funding.

Members discussed a monthly range for an interim, with benefits about a fifth of base, and a three-month contract cost.

what_happened.line: The Select Board adopted a new public communications policy, section 2.13, on a 3 to 2 vote.
The board took no action on the Flat Hill Road speed petition and will wait for a new traffic study, with another after the bridge reopens in October.
The board agreed the town manager job posting will say salary is commensurate with experience, with no range stated.
The board approved a draft letter to the state representative on Chapter 70 and non-regional bus funding.
The board declared 925 Mass Ave surplus and offered it for sale with a preference for renovation, with one abstention.

why_it_matters: The communications policy sets how the board speaks publicly, and the vote on it was split.
The Flat Hill Road speed limit stays as it is until the traffic studies are done, so residents there should expect a wait.
The town manager search and the Chapter 70 and bus-funding letter bear on who runs town government and on how much state help the schools and the tax bill get.
watch_next: The new traffic study on Flat Hill Road, and a second one after the bridge reopens in October.
The workshop on FY2025 Select Board goals, deferred to a future meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all eight non-procedural votes and on the main decisions. Most differences are caption errors in figures and names. The one thing to check is the permanent town manager salary range, where our captions give figures that do not match the range the official minutes print.
